solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old Violet, one easily manipulated by church

blocks.note: a pawn is a person used by others for their own ends
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An old woman called Violet is pushed around by her parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital V dresses the flower up as a woman's name; 'Old' marks the word as an archaic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawnce is an obsolete name for the pansy, a garden flower of the viola family.

clue.text: Fables bringing god-talk to Roman caves

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
chat is informal talk
antra is the Latin plural of antrum, a cave or cavity

explanation.surface: Stories that carry talk of the gods into Roman caves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' signals a Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panchatantra is an ancient Sanskrit collection of animal stories with moral lessons.

clue.text: Supply of minimal old money? Much more needed to make you this!

definitions.text: Much more needed to make you this!

blocks.note: a well is a source of supply, as of water
taken as written
F is the farthing, the smallest old British coin, or the old French franc

explanation.surface: A tiny sum of old money will not go far towards making you rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the second sentence: a farthing (a quarter of an old penny) is far short of making anyone comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well off means being comfortably wealthy, which a single farthing could never achieve.

clue.text: Compound of arsenic is something insoluble

indicators.note: a compound mixes its ingredients together, so the letters are combined in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemistry fact: an arsenic compound will not dissolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' reads as chemistry, which is apt, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerasin is the part of cherry-tree gum that swells in water but does not dissolve.

clue.text: Garden's retreat I found in London city area

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so these pieces sit within another

blocks.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
a den is a private retreat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden hideaway discovered in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garden is Eden, so 'Garden's' means belonging to Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Edenic means relating to the Garden of Eden, or paradisal.

clue.text: Greek mathematician producing some fine stuff

blocks.note: first meaning: ... of Alexandria, a geometer of the fourth century
second meaning: the tuft of fine hairs on a seed such as a dandelion's

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek scholar turns out some excellent work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine stuff' reads as praise for the mathematician's output, but it means literally thin, downy material.
explanation.definitionFit: A pappus is the feathery ring of hairs that helps seeds like thistledown drift on the wind; Pappus is also a Greek geometer's name.

clue.text: Classical art is in a strong position, according to some

definitions.text: a strong position, according to some

blocks.note: ars is Latin for art
taken as written

explanation.surface: Classical art is said to be in a commanding position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to some' is needed because Greek and Latin prosody use arsis for opposite syllables, weak and stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: In English usage arsis is the stressed syllable of a metrical foot, though some use it for the unstressed one.

clue.text: Prime minister in hole with time running short

indicators.note: something running short is cut down, here to its opening letter

blocks.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
the first letter of time

explanation.surface: A prime minister in trouble as time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitt the Elder and Pitt the Younger were both British prime ministers in the eighteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: William Pitt, father and son, each led Britain's government as premier.

clue.text: Power given to senior French revolutionary

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
aîné is French for elder or senior

explanation.surface: Authority is handed to a senior figure of the French Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French revolutionary' reads as one phrase, but 'French' belongs with 'senior'. Thomas Paine supported both the American and French revolutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Paine, author of Common Sense and Rights of Man, was a radical champion of revolution.

clue.text: Bird that could be concealed in grass and heather

indicators.note: could be means the letters might form something else if reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird that might hide away in grass and heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concealed in' tempts a hidden-word hunt, but no run of letters works; the letters of grass and heather together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The sage thrasher is a small grey North American songbird of sagebrush country.

clue.text: Learner in Lincoln with radiance effusing

indicators.note: effusing means pouring out, so the letters spill and come out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar name
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A student in the city of Lincoln glows with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city but is the American president.
explanation.definitionFit: An abecedarian is someone still learning the alphabet, a beginner at the very start of schooling.

clue.text: Collecting what dogs unfortunately leave on heather?

blocks.note: poo is excrement
ling is common heather

explanation.surface: Gathering up the mess dogs leave on the moor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, one piece 'on' another sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooling means gathering resources or things together into a common store.

clue.text: Manfully opposing wild bear with sort of trap

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run loose into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a sting is a police operation set up to trap criminals

explanation.surface: A hunter bravely confronts a wild bear armed only with a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To breast something is to face it head on, chest forward, as in breasting the waves.

clue.text: Potato to be withdrawn, root for extraction

indicators.note: in a down answer the root is the bottom end, and extraction pulls it out

blocks.note: aloof means distant and reserved

explanation.surface: A potato is pulled from the menu, its root marked for removal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' sounds like vegetable talk, apt for a potato, but it is the last letter of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloo is the Hindi word for potato, familiar from dishes like aloo gobi.

clue.text: Young player, one that's solid and dull

definitions.note: describes the answer, a noun, rather than naming it

blocks.note: a colt is a young or novice sportsman
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A young sportsman who is dependable but unexciting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a steady but boring player; the last three words describe a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Coltan is a dull black metallic ore, a solid mineral mined for tantalum used in electronics.

clue.text: Unexplained sensations a number got with repeated viewings of French art

blocks.note: taken as written
no is short for number
es is French for 'art' as in thou art, given twice

explanation.surface: Strange feelings caught by someone repeatedly viewing French paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old verb, thou art; French for it is tu es.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoesis is a state of pure sensation or feeling without understanding or interpretation.

clue.text: Noises from angry drivers? I'm annoyed!

blocks.note: first meaning: blasts on car horns
second meaning: a Scots exclamation of impatience

explanation.surface: Motorists sound off, and someone shouts their irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots interjection 'hoots!' expresses annoyance or disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Car horns give hoots, and Scots use 'hoots' as an exclamation of irritation or protest.

clue.text: Element of most entertaining show rarely encountered

indicators.note: an element is a component part, so the letters are just a part of the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a hugely entertaining show that one seldom sees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely encountered' marks the word as rare, not the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostent is a rare word for display or ostentation, sharing its root with ostensible.

clue.text: Grass area by which sits an ignorant fellow

blocks.note: Alf is Australian slang for an uncultured, loutish man
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A lawn where a dim man is sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: ALF sits beside the A. An Alf, in Australian usage, is a boorish, unsophisticated man.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfa is esparto, a tough grass grown in North Africa for making paper and rope.

clue.text: Relaxed party by an Italian lake

blocks.note: Lake Como is in northern Italy
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A laid-back celebration beside an Italian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Comodo is a musical direction, Italian for leisurely.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, comodo instructs the player to perform at an easy, unhurried pace.

clue.text: Fellow needs medical professional after swallowing one plant

indicators.note: whatever swallows something takes it inside, so a piece goes within these letters

blocks.note: a man is a fellow
doc is short for doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man needs a doctor after swallowing a poisonous plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandioc is a variant spelling of manioc, the cassava plant with starchy roots.

clue.text: Mineral is oddly crushed

indicators.note: crushed things are broken up, so the letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mineral that crumbles in a peculiar way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'crushed' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dysodil is a foul-smelling, flaky brown coal or lignite that burns with a fetid odour.

clue.text: Expression of regret from one in indulgent mode losing daughter

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
acting fondly is acting with doting indulgence
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A lament from a doting parent who has lost their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: 'If only' introduces a wish that things had gone differently, a common way of voicing regret.

clue.text: Material for old music-hall performer

blocks.note: first meaning: an open, gauze-like woven fabric
second meaning: Dan ..., the Victorian comedian

explanation.surface: Fresh comic material for a veteran variety act.
explanation.walkthrough: Music hall was Victorian British variety theatre, where Dan Leno was a star comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Leno is a light cotton weave used for curtains, and also the stage name of comic Dan Leno.

clue.text: Thus gives way and errs, resulting in deadly sin?

indicators.note: to err is to go astray, so the letters wander out of place

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters set aside

explanation.surface: Giving in to temptation and going wrong leads to mortal sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the answer plus AND, rearranged, makes DEADLY SIN; so the letters of deadly sin, less A, N, D, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way, as traffic yields to oncoming cars.

clue.text: You must be occupying doctor as one changing colour

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
ye is the archaic plural form of you

explanation.surface: A patient is told to see the doctor about a change of complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer's trade is altering the colour of cloth or yarn with dyes.

clue.text: Source of beef joint when there's nothing to be eaten

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside whatever eats it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the ankle is a joint of the leg
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cut of beef served when the cupboard is otherwise bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts towards a roast, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ankole is a breed of long-horned East African cattle raised for meat.

clue.text: Tree providing wooden tub for storing rock

indicators.note: a tub used for storing holds things within it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a kit is a small wooden tub or pail
aa is rough, clinkery lava

explanation.surface: A tree whose timber makes tubs for keeping stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Aa is a Hawaiian term for rough, jagged lava.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiaat is a southern African hardwood tree, also called bloodwood, prized for furniture.

clue.text: A slip — wrong units of money

indicators.note: wrong means not correct, so the letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cashier's slip-up gets the money wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The lipa was a Croatian coin, one hundredth of a kuna.

clue.text: Tree in US city idiot knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: NY is New York
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: In an American city, a fool is knocked down by a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyssa is the tupelo genus, North American trees valued for honey and autumn colour.

clue.text: Muslims needing something to put off extremists

indicators.note: putting off the extremes means sending away the letters at each end

blocks.note: summat is northern English dialect for something

explanation.surface: A community of believers needs a way to deter radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Summat is a northern English dialect form of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The umma is the worldwide community of Muslims, bound together by faith.

clue.text: Journalist cooks bits of certain plants

blocks.note: ed is short for editor
a cook does the vegetables or does a meal

explanation.surface: A reporter prepares food from parts of some plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddoes are the starchy corms of the taro plant, eaten as a root vegetable.

clue.text: Vagrant by old pool to jump up and down

blocks.note: a tramp is a homeless wanderer
O is the abbreviation for old
a lin, or linn, is a pool below a waterfall

explanation.surface: A tramp leaps about beside an old swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: Lin is a Scots and northern word for a waterfall or the pool beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampolin, a variant of trampoline, is also a verb meaning to bounce on a sprung mat.

clue.text: I am called to change, becoming member of religious order

indicators.note: a change of order rearranges the letters of the words before it

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feels a calling to change their life and join a monastic order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called' suggests a religious vocation, and 'to' seems to belong with 'change', but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camaldolites are a Benedictine order of hermit monks founded at Camaldoli in Italy.

clue.text: A request to keep alcohol-free bringing dubious rebuke

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so these letters hold another piece inside

blocks.note: taken as written
to ask is to request
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A request to stay off the drink earns an uncertain telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' flags a doubtful word: attask appears in Shakespeare but may be a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Attask is a Shakespearean verb for taking someone to task, a word whose authenticity is questioned.

clue.text: What could get molars finally clear possibly?

definitions.text: What could get molars finally clear possibly?

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word just before it
possibly suggests one of the possible arrangements of the letters

blocks.note: the last letter of molars
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what tool might get one's back teeth clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist's scaler scrapes tartar off teeth, so it is exactly what would clear molars.
